correctness.rationale: Hilbert inequality bounds the classical (m+n−1)^-1 matrix; μ=c/(j+1)+r_j with O((j+1)^-1−δ) yields an HS Hankel remainder. The exact commutator matrix (m^-α−n^-α)μ_{m+n−2} is HS for α>0. The log ratio bound |m^-α−n^-α|≤α|log(m/n)| and fixed-s ratio square-sum O(s) show the remainder changes squared HS norm by O(α²). Replacing discrete denominator (m+n−1)^-2 and then the lattice sum by its [1,∞)^2 integral costs O(α²) via summable derivative bounds. Exact substitution yields (1/α)∫_0^1(1−u^α)²/(1+u)²du = α∫ log²u/(1+u)²du+O(α²)=π²α/6+O(α²). Beta-integral tail estimate gives density w(1) specialization. Independent direct numerical quadratures returned 1.644934066848 ≈π²/6; the analytic estimates, not finite sections, establish infinite HS limit.

value.rationale: Canonical Hilbert Hankel operators are borderline bounded and noncompact, while Dα→I strongly. Their commutator has a singular but exactly quantified √α Hilbert–Schmidt norm cusp, and the leading coefficient persists for arbitrary polynomially smaller moment tails. This natural endpoint operator invariant and nontrivial universality are not mere rewording of matrix Schatten membership.

limitations: Only polynomial moment tails δ>0 and α↓0; for c=0 O(α²) but no coefficient.
Possible equivalent Mellin commutator literature not completely ruled out.
No other Schatten classes or singular-value distributions proved.
